messages:
Samir (Support): @BrightBuild — heads up, we got a customer escalation: spike in 429s + higher latency starting ~09:18 UTC on /v1/generate-chat. Can you paste a failing response if available?
BrightBuild-CS: Here — 429 with body 'quota_exceeded' and headers: X-RateLimit-Limit:600, X-RateLimit-Remaining:0, X-RateLimit-Reset:1690002000. Correlation id: trace-4e7a9b. Happens during our nightly prewarm job.
Priya (SRE): thx. @Marco I'm going to look at throttle logs. Can you capture the trace id in the throttles index? We log event_type=throttle with customer, route, model, tokens, burst_used.
Marco (Runtime): got the id, pulling logs... quick summary: lots of throttle events for customer_id=brightbuild-prod between 09:18-09:22. Route=/v1/generate-chat, model=redwood-large-v1. Observed tokens/min average ~120k, burst consumption peaked at ~600k in a short window. Looks like they hit burst allotment then exhausted steady tokens.
Olga (Product): Do they use Hosted standard or Dedicated? That changes the burst policy.
BrightBuild-CS: Hosted standard. No dedicated pool. We run a bulk prewarm to generate context embeddings, which is likely the traffic pattern.
Samir (Support): Are there dashboards we can hand them to inspect?
Priya (SRE): Yes — check these internal dashboards: "Limits / Throttles by customer" (panel: throttle_rate by customer), "Route token usage" (split by route -> model), and "Burst consumption heatmap". Look at 09:00-09:30 UTC. Also see alert throttle_spike_high triggered at 09:21.
Marco (Runtime): note on implementation: rate-limiter is leaky-bucket per-customer per-route. Default burst window = 60s, standard-tier burst tokens = 500k. We logged burst_used=600k so they exceeded the allowed burst and then hit steady quota limits -> 429.
BrightBuild-CS: Is there a recommended repro we can run to confirm?
Samir (Support): Repro steps for support: 1) Do a 1-minute ramp to ~2x typical p95 QPS against /v1/generate-chat using their API key. 2) Capture X-Request-Id + correlation_id. 3) If fails, attach sample response headers and any trace ids.
BrightBuild-CS: quick curl we used: ```curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"redwood-large-v1","input":"hello"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate-chat```
Priya (SRE): For attribution queries, run: ```sum by (customer, route, model) (rate(throttle_events_total[5m]))``` and compare with request rate: ```sum by (customer, route) (rate(api_requests_total[5m]))```. Also check traces with tag throttle=true in Jaeger/tempo.
Marco (Runtime): Logs show repeated rapid retries from their prewarm job which amplified burst usage. Two remediation paths: 1) short-term - ask customer to add exponential backoff + jitter and lower burst; 2) medium-term - increase their burst allotment or move to Dedicated. We can also enable transient burst buffer for enterprise customers.
Olga (Product): Can we offer a temporary quota bump while we work through the pattern?
Priya (SRE): I can approve a short-lived bump if Security signs off. Need a ticket with exact customer_id and length. I'll also check whether the transient burst buffer is safe to enable for hosted standard.
Samir (Support): For observability/alerting suggestions for customers: set alerts for throttle_rate/customer > 5% of requests over 1m, X-RateLimit-Remaining == 0 occurrences > 10 in 5m, and token_rate per model > model_profile.max_tokens_per_min * 0.9.
Marco (Runtime): Also useful query to correlate throttles to model: ```topk(10, sum by (model, customer) (rate(throttle_events_total[5m])))``` and a join on request traces to get sample payload sizes.
BrightBuild-CS: We've attached two traces and the CI job logs in ticket #4567. Any immediate workaround to reduce 429s?
Marco (Runtime): Short-term: throttle the prewarm job to ~70% of observed average and add exponential backoff honoring Retry-After header. Mid-term: consider Dedicated capacity for predictable throughput. Also recommend caching/prefix KV for embeddings to reduce tokens churn.
Priya (SRE): Runbook checklist for support triage: 1) collect correlation ids + X-Request-Id 2) query throttle_events_total for customer in window 3) check route and model tags and burst_used field 4) inspect alert history for throttle_spike_high 5) propose mitigation (client-side backoff, quota bump, dedicated)
Marco (Runtime): I'll save a dashboard and runbook snippet. Saved dashboard link: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/slug/throttles-by-customer-abc123 (internal). Runbook snippet to attach: ```If throttle spike: 1) collect trace id 2) query throttle_events_total{customer="X"} 3) check route/model tags 4) confirm burst_used% and tokens/min 5) recommend quota bump or backoff```
rate-limit-bot: Alert: throttle_spike_high for brightbuild-prod — triggered at 09:21:14, current_rate=0.062 (6.2%) :rotating_light:
Samir (Support): Action items: Marco -> post dashboard + runbook to ticket, Priya -> check if transient burst buffer / temp bump ok, Olga -> update customer-facing doc about attributing throttles and dashboards. I'll update ticket #4567 and follow up. :+1:
BrightBuild-CS: Thanks — we'll throttle our job and re-run repro, attaching new correlation ids. Ping us if you need more logs. :wave:
